_note: PIN CLUSTERING - without it five hundred pins is an unusable smear, and every mapping app hits that wall. The algorithm is pinned here rather than left to each platform's library, because MKClusterAnnotation, maps-utils and Supercluster group differently at the same zoom and a screenshot test becomes impossible. THE ALGORITHM: project each pin to normalised web-mercator world space, multiply by the world size at the CLUSTER LEVEL, and take the integer cell of side clusterRadius. THE STABILITY RULE: the cluster level is floor(zoom), never zoom. A continuous grid slides continuously, so at zoom 12.37 a pin sits in one cell and at 12.38 in the next, and markers visibly flicker while the user pinches. Quantising the level means membership is IDENTICAL for every fractional zoom inside an integer level and only changes when the level changes - which is exactly what the `stability` section asserts. ORDER is row-major by cell (cy, then cx) so all three renderers emit the same nodes in the same sequence and the same ids, which is what stops marker churn on redraw. A cell holding one pin is NOT a cluster. A cluster's coordinate is the mean of its members in WORLD space, not the mean of their latitudes. expansionZoom is the first level at which the members stop sharing a cell, which is what on:clusterTap zooms to.

membership._note: One nine-pin set, three fractional zooms inside level 12 plus the level change at 13.

stability._note: The flicker test stated as an assertion: identical node ids across a fractional zoom sweep inside one level, and a DIFFERENT set once the level changes.

scale._note: Five hundred pins across five metros on a deterministic lattice. The assertion is the ordered (id, count) digest - identical on all three renderers, at three zooms.
